summary: Kootenai NF lookout: a c.1910 pole platform, a 1927 log cabin, and the present timber tower built in 1957, now rented by reservation.

facts.design: Present treated-timber tower with L-4 cab (built 1957); earlier 45-foot pole platform (about 1910) and L-6 cupola log cabin (1927)

access.note: Rented through the Recreation.gov Recreation Rental program, typically late June to late September. Reached by car; access depends on weather; high-clearance vehicle recommended.

visit.trail_note: Yaak Falls is a short drive off Yaak Highway 508. Hiking trails in the Yaak Area and the Northwest Peaks Scenic Area are nearby.

facts.agency: US Forest Service, Kootenai National Forest

events.note: Observation point with a 45-foot pole platform tower developed on the site
Pole platform replaced by a log cabin with L-6 cupola
Present 30-foot treated timber tower with L-4 cab built

evidence.quote: Developed about 1910 with a 45' pole platform tower, and replaced in 1927 by a log cabin with L-6 cupola, the present 30' treated timber tower with L-4 cab was built in 1957.

corrections.why: The brief's 13.7 m (45 ft) is the about-1910 pole platform. NHLR and firelookout.com describe the present tower as 30 feet (9.1 m). Recreation.gov says 26 feet; see resolved_conflicts.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and firelookout.com give the present tower as 30 feet. Recreation.gov says the cabin sits atop a 26-foot tower. The record uses 30 feet (9.1 m) and does not explain the 26-foot figure.

sources.title: MT. Baldy-Buckhorn Ridge, Kootenai National Forest
Baldy Mtn. (Buckhorn Baldy) Fire Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: The history (about 1910 pole platform, 1927 cabin, 1957 tower) agrees across all three sources. Height conflict: NHLR and firelookout.com say 30 feet, Recreation.gov says 26 feet. Elevation: NHLR says 6,531 ft (1,991 m); Recreation.gov and firelookout.com say 6,529 ft. The record uses the brief's elevation of 1990.6 m. No staffing information and no notable fires appear in these three sources. Firelookout.com credits photos to the U.S. Forest Service and Gary Weber, but no image URLs were read, so none are recorded. Reservation dates should be checked on Recreation.gov before publishing.
